integrator_questions: With this unchanged geometry, which bend or section produces the peak error, and does the controller's kd or kp setting shift that peak?
Does the 12 mm five-sensor array lose the line on the slalom (line_loss_events 2)? If so, would a 16 mm sensor size be worth testing in a later design?
Are there controller changes that bring max_error below 0.06 m on the s-bend without losing oval progress?

intent: Deliver the best measured geometry (iteration 7, score 73.33) unchanged for the final race. Five 12 mm sensors on a 12 mm pitch sit at the 0.08 m lookahead maximum, with a 0.12 m track, 0.03 m wheels, 1.0 kg mass, 0.12 m body width and 0.18 m body length. Expected: a score near 73 on the development tracks, with the same off-track pattern (max_error about 0.06 m), and the best available chance of progress on the unseen track.
learning: Lookahead, track, mass and wheel radius each show a measured optimum near the current values, so the baseline is locally tuned. Sensor size (16 mm) and sensor pitch remain untested in isolation, and would be the next single-variable tests if there were another iteration. The final-track score depends on whether this geometry generalises beyond the development tracks, which the unseen race will show.
rationale: Scores by iteration: the 80 mm sensor row at 0.12 m track, 0.8 kg, 0.03 m wheels and 12 mm sensors gave 69.18. Raising mass to 1.0 kg gave 73.33 (iteration 7), the best score so far. Mass 1.2 kg fell to 60.14 (iteration 8), so mass has turned over near 1.0 kg. Wheel radius 0.035 m fell to 64.78 (iteration 9), and 0.025 m gave 72.71 (iteration 10). That puts the radius optimum at or near 0.03 m, with 0.025 m only slightly worse. Lookahead (40, 60, 80 mm), track (0.10, 0.12, 0.14 m) and mass have each been tested one at a time, and the best value of each sits at or near the current design. Every run ends off track with max_error of 0.060 to 0.066 m, just above the 0.06 m limit, while rms_error stays at 0.02 to 0.03 m. The failure is a transient peak on bends. Body width cannot move the limit, so it stays at 0.12 m. The sensor size and pitch effects are still unisolated (iteration 1 confounded them with mass and track). This is the final iteration, and the unseen-track race is scored, so I am not spending the race on an untested change. I am delivering the best measured geometry (iteration 7) unchanged. Any further change would be a gamble with no evidence and no iteration left to recover from it.
